sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11027 of 2023

Applicant :- Shani @ Chandra Prakash
Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. Thru.

The Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of Home, U.P. Civil Sec
Counsel for Applicant :- Neeraj Kumar Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1. Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including up-to-date case diary and charge sheet in this case has also been submitted.

2. Heard Shri Neeraj Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Shani @ Chandra Prakash for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 26 of 2022, under Sections 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Leelapur, District Pratapgarh,
during trial.

sentences.text:
On being recovered, the statement of the prosecutrix/victim was recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., wherein she has not imputed any allegations against the applicant and in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated that she had left her home on her own and had accompanied the applicant and the applicant has neither enticed her nor has done anything wrong with her and she had accompanied the applicant with her free will, wish and volition.
6.

It is vehemently submitted that since no allegation of any kind has been levelled by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. against the applicant in fact no offence could be attributed to the applicant.

7. It is further submitted that the charge sheet after thorough investigation was filed in this case under Sections 363, 366, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(da), (dha) and 3(2)(v) of S.C./S.T. Act and the applicant had earlier approached this Court (High Court) by filing a Criminal Appeal No. 2928 of 2022 and vide order dated 28.02.2023 passed therein he was granted bail.
However, during the course of trial after in-chief-examination of the prosecutrix was recorded before the trial Court as P.W.-1.

The trial Court appears to have framed the charges under relevant provisions of the P.O.C.S.O. Act also and when an application for bail in the added sections were moved before the Special Court, the same has been rejected.

8. It is vehemently submitted that since after filing of the charge sheet applicant was granted bail by this Court (High Court) no opportunity was available to the Special Court to reject the bail application of the applicant in added penal sections as this Court (High Court) after perusing and taking into consideration all the relevant material which was collected during the course of investigation has granted the facility of bail to the applicant.

9. It is also submitted that apart from being lodged in jail in this case earlier in the added sections wherein the charge has been framed by the Trial Court/Special Court, the applicant is now languishing in jail in this case in added penal sections since 29.08.2022.
He is not having any criminal history and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
10. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that in the statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has not levelled any kind of allegations against the instant applicant.

The age of the prosecutrix in the F.I.R. as well as in her statements is shown as 19 years, while her bone-age has been determined as 17 years and as per her educational credentials her date of birth is shown to be as 12.06.2006.

Having regard to the contradictions evident with regard to the age of the prosecutrix the same may be better adjudicated/determined by the trial Court during the course of trial after providing an opportunity to led evidence to the parties. Admittedly the applicant had earlier been released on bail in this case by this Court in the penal sections wherein the charge sheet was submitted after thorough Shani @ Chandra Prakash vs The State Of U.P. Thru.

sentences.text: while this Court has granted bail to the applicant after taking into consideration all the relevant material which was collected by the investigating officer during the course of investigation.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 29.08.2022 without any criminal antecedents and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

13. Let the accused/applicant- Shani @ Chandra Prakash involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
